Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:

   The user's single request (verbatim): "Tui's overlay is stuck on the menu: picking a game never actually launches a run, and the window chrome around the board is dead too, so the minimize-to-pill button, the resize toggle, the How to Play guide and the sign-out confirmation all do nothing. Wire the whole session back up: starting a run, pausing when the agent needs you and resuming, restarting mid-run, and ending a shift cleanly, plus the window minimize/restore/resize behavior the README and the on-screen buttons describe, including saving progress so a run can resume on the next launch."

   Concretely this means restoring, in `/app/overlay`:
   - Starting a run (menu → variations → Enter/click launches; deep-link `gamepigeon:launch` and `?game=`/`?variation=` in preview; Resume button; `resumeLastGame` setting).
   - Pausing when the agent needs you and resuming (host `gamepigeon:pause`/`:resume`, the `#return-prompt` "Paused" card and its four buttons).
   - Restarting mid-run (`r`, `[data-restart]`, in-canvas restart) with README's exact semantics: throw the save away, brand-new randomized seed that is never the replaced run's seed, empty action log.
   - Ending a shift cleanly (in-canvas "menu", `#inline-back`, `#return-menu`, host `gamepigeon:reset`) leaving the save byte-for-byte intact so it can be resumed later.
   - Window chrome: `#resize` toggle (600×850 ↔ 830×900, ↗/↙), `#hide` → 144×48 pill (`body[data-mode="pill"]`), `#pill` click → restore (floor 500×700, centered), `#shutdown`, titlebar drag, pill drag.
   - How to Play dialog and the sign-out confirmation dialog.
   - Saving progress to `localStorage` so a run resumes on the next launch.

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - Bun + TypeScript; Tauri v2 native shell (`tauri/src/main.rs`) with an HTML/Phaser overlay in `overlay/`.
   - `overlay/dist/index.html` is the checked-in source of all static markup + CSS (not generated); `scripts/build-overlay-web.ts` bundles only `overlay/app.ts` and `overlay/restaurant-arena-preview.ts` into `overlay/dist/`.
   - Host→webview events via `window.eval`: `gamepigeon:launch` (`CustomEvent` detail `{game, variation}`), `:resume`, `:pause`, `:reset`, `:auth-success` (detail `{email}`), `:auth-error` (string), `:sync-error`, `:sync-success`, `:worker-budget`.
   - Tauri commands available: `shutdown, read_settings, write_settings, read_worker_model_config, complete_worker_model, cancel_worker_model, record_analytics_event, append_local_score, read_local_scores, queue_recording_chunks, read_update_flag, read_update_plan, run_plugin_update, read_auth_session, read_sync_error, start_auth_login, open_login_url, cancel_auth_login, sign_out`.
   - Gym-style `Game` contract (`reset(seed)`/`step(action)`/`state()`/`score()`), `PlayableGame` adds `isOver()`, `hasWon()`, optional `tickMs()`, `keymap`, `checkpointState()`.
   - Two competing "advancers" for the shift clock: `WorkerOrchestrator` (live model crew, drives its own `game.step("tick")`) vs. a local `setTimeout` tick loop; `tickMs()` returns 0 whenever the engine wants the clock still.
   - Recording: `StoredOverlayTrace` journal in `localStorage` under `gamepigeon:recording:<gameId>`, sealed chunks flushed every 5s, `EpisodeEndReason` ∈ `game_over|won|lost|user_quit|restart|timeout|client_closed|engine_error`.

```

In the overlay: arrow keys or WASD to move, `Enter` to select, `r` to restart, `Esc` or `q` to hide. Drag the top bar to move the window; use the expand control to resize it.

### Session save

Every launch keeps exactly one `SavedGame` record in `localStorage` under
`gamepigeon.arcade.active-game.v1` (`overlay/persistence.ts`): `gameId`,
`gameVersion`, `variationId`, the run's `seed`, and the ordered `actions`
taken so far, so the same run can be rebuilt action-by-action on the next
launch. The two ways a run stops mid-shift treat that record differently:

- **Ending a shift back to the menu** (the in-canvas "menu" control, or a
  host `gamepigeon:reset`) leaves the save exactly as it was. The seed and
  the action log are untouched, so resuming later replays the identical run.
- **Restarting mid-run** (`r`, or the in-canvas "restart" control) throws the
  save away and opens a brand-new run of the same game and variation: a
  freshly randomized `seed` -- never the seed of the run it replaces -- and
  an empty action log. Restart means "start over with a new run," not
  "replay the same seed again"; only a resumed/recovered launch reuses a
  stored seed.

### Window sizes

The native Tauri frame — and the browser preview, which mirrors it pixel for pixel — uses these exact logical sizes:

| State | Trigger | Width × height |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Compact (default) | boot, or the expand control while expanded | 600 × 850 |
| Expanded | the expand control while compact | 830 × 900 |
| Minimized pill | Hide (`Esc` / `q` / the hide button) | 144 × 48 |
| Restored floor | clicking the pill again | back to the compact size, never smaller than 500 × 700 |

These are exactly the values `overlay/tauri-bridge.ts` exports as `COMPACT_SIZE`, `EXPANDED_SIZE`, `PILL_SIZE`, and `MIN_SIZE`, and what `overlay/preview.html` frames the browser preview at.

## Install: local vs. global
=== 190-215
bun run claude:dev        # Claude Code
bun run codex:dev         # Codex CLI
bun run antigravity:dev   # Antigravity (agy)
```

`SessionStart` snaps a still-running overlay back to the menu (without popping the window open) so a new session never resumes mid-game, `UserPromptSubmit` shows the overlay, `Stop` pauses it with an `Enter` shortcut back to the coding prompt, and `SessionEnd` shuts down the helper.

Antigravity has none of those four events — it fires `PreToolUse`, `PostToolUse`, `PreInvocation`, `PostInvocation`, and `Stop`, and drops any other key without an error. `scripts/antigravity-hook.ts` maps the same lifecycle onto `PreInvocation` + `Stop`; see [docs/harness-antigravity.md](docs/harness-antigravity.md).

To enable the hooks for the normal `claude` command, install the GitHub marketplace once:

```bash
claude plugin marketplace add Trolleroof/tui-gamepigeon
claude plugin install tui-gamepigeon@tui-gamepigeon --scope user
```

Claude Code does not silently install plugin updates. Tui uses a WOZ-style detect-and-nudge flow instead (see **Auto-updates** below).

The generated adapters live at `~/.codex/skills/arcade`, `~/.claude/skills/arcade`, and `~/.config/opencode/commands/arcade.md`; all execute `scripts/overlay.ts` from this checkout. The installer refuses to replace an unrelated command with the same name. Press `Esc` or `q` to hide the game, drag its top bar to move it, and use the expand button to resize it.

## Auto-updates
=== 285-305

## Interaction traces

The recording layer under `src/recording/` durably journals episodes under `~/.tui-gamepigeon/recordings/` and splits them into immutable upload chunks. Every schema-v2 event includes `event_id`, `user_id`, `chunk_id`, and `game_id`.

- Policy-visible events preserve input impulses, timing, score/reward changes, and episode completion.
- Privileged engine checkpoints and realized random effects support deterministic replay without leaking hidden state into policy input.
- Local writes continue when upload is disabled or temporarily unavailable; pending chunks retry on later sessions.
- Completed games also enter a separate durable score outbox. Quits, restarts, and client shutdowns never submit a score.
- `~/.tui-gamepigeon/recordings/` is the complete, local source for BC datasets. Syncing a chunk stores and queues it in the cloud; it does not make it retrievable through the API. Completed episodes are now also written to R2 as Parquet, but that corpus is partial and not yet indexed. See [Where synced traces land](#where-synced-traces-land).

## Local score history

Every naturally completed overlay game appends one JSON object to
`~/.tui-gamepigeon/scores/history.jsonl`, even without a network connection.
The directory is user-only (`0700`) and the JSONL file is `0600`. Quits,
restarts, and shutdowns do not create entries.

Each schema-v1 row contains `game_id`, `game_type`, `variation_id`, `score`,
`success`, `completed_at` (the game-end timestamp), `duration_ms`, and
`platform`, plus the resulting `personal_best` and `high_score_updated`.

lines: +// The frame only ever takes the four sizes `tauri-bridge.ts` exports (README,
+// "Window sizes"). Two of them are the expand toggle. The third is the pill,
+// which is deliberately smaller than the window's own minimum, so minimizing
+// has to lower that minimum before the pill size can land — Tauri clamps
+// `setSize` against `setMinSize` — and restoring has to put it back.
+/** The bridge hands back the real Tauri size under Tauri and a stand-in in preview. */
+/** Put the window at whichever frame the expand control currently describes. */
+    // A frame we cannot set is no reason to lose the session behind it.
+ * The titlebar's ↗/↙. `defaultWindowSize` is the *default*, so toggling is a
+ * choice about this session and is not written back over the setting.
+ * Collapse to the handheld pill. The shift keeps its state — `isHeld` stops the
+ * clock rather than ending the run — so clicking the pill drops the player back
+ * into the same tick they left.
+    // Keep `data-mode="pill"`: the app is already hidden, and a window stuck
+    // at the old size showing a pill is still recoverable by clicking it.
+ * Back from the pill. The frame returns to the size the player was last at —
+ * compact unless they had expanded it — never below `MIN_SIZE`, and centered,
+ * because the pill may have been dragged to an edge the full window cannot fit.
+ * The pill is one target for two gestures: a click reopens, a drag moves the
+ * window. Once `startDragging` hands the pointer to the compositor no click
+ * arrives at all, so the flag only has to survive the gestures that do click.
+  let origin: { x: number; y: number } | null = null;
+// ── Holds: the agent's pause, the pill, and the dialogs ───────────────
+ * Project {@link session} onto the DOM, then re-pick the advancer.
+ * Only called on a transition, so moving focus here is safe: whatever card just
+ * took over the screen is what `Enter`/`Esc` should reach.
+// Two things can move the clock and never both: a live crew, which ends each
+// of its own rounds with a `step("tick")`, or the local timer for a shift with
+// no crew attached. `tickMs() === 0` is the engine saying *hold* — before the
+// doors open, on an open decision, once the shift is over — and nothing
+    if (screen !== "game" || !game || replaying || gameEnded || game.isOver() || isHeld(session)) return;

steps.message:
The session is wired back up in `overlay/app.ts`, with the reusable rules split into `overlay/pause-state.ts` and covered by tests.

**Starting a run** — `beginRun()` is the single entry point: it closes any prior run, picks the variation, `reset()`s on a fresh seed, writes the `SavedGame`, mints an overlay trace, attaches the worker orchestrator, and captures `game.started`. It's reached from Enter/click on the variation list, `data-variation-index`, the menu Resume button, the host `gamepigeon:launch` deep link, `?game=`/`?variation=` in the browser preview, and the `resumeLastGame` setting on boot. A `launch` that arrives while the sign-in gate is up is stashed in `pendingLaunch` and replayed after `enterArcade()` rather than skipping the gate.

**Pausing and resuming** — the three things that stop a shift (the agent's hold, the pill, an open dialog) are tracked separately in `pause-state.ts` instead of one boolean, so closing How to Play doesn't forget you were paused and minimizing doesn't leave the clock running. `syncSession()` derives what's on screen from that state; `syncSchedulers()` derives whether the clock runs, gating *both* advancers (the local `setTimeout` loop and `WorkerOrchestrator`) on `tickMs() > 0` so worker turns stop while a decision card is open. "Back to coding" clears the agent hold and minimizes — the pill keeps the shift held, so clicking it returns you to the same tick.

**Restarting** — `restartRun()` submits the abandoned trace with reason `restart`, clears the save, and starts over on `randomSeed(previousSeed)`, which never returns the seed it replaced. Bound to `r`, `[data-restart]`, and the in-canvas restart.

**Ending a shift** — `endShiftToMenu()` tears down the run and leaves `localStorage` untouched, so the menu's Resume picks it back up. `endGame()` is the only path that submits a score (clamped at 0, since the engine can price a shift negative and the Rust validator rejects negatives) and the only one that clears the save. Natural-end detection lives in one place, at the end of `drawGame()`, so interventions and pass-rounds reach it too.

**Window chrome** — `#resize` toggles 600×850 ↔ 830×900 with the ↗/↙ glyph, `#hide` lowers the min-size floor before dropping to the 144×48 pill (the floor is 500×700, above the pill — `tauri-bridge.test.ts` pins that ordering constraint), `#pill` restores and re-centers, and pill drags past 3px suppress the restore click. `#shutdown`, titlebar drag, How to Play and the sign-out confirmation are all bound; a failed sign-out flashes "Could not sign out" and keeps the dialog open.

`bun run typecheck` passes clean and `bun run build:overlay:web` is rebuilt. `bun run test:overlay` is **200 pass / 2 fail**, and both failures predate these changes and are in code I didn't touch:

- `scripts/plugin-update.test.ts:241` "keeps the Claude marketplace install on its own updater" — expects `updateMethod: "claude-marketplace"`, gets `"unknown"`. Environment-dependent install detection, nothing to do with the overlay.
- `overlay/recording.test.ts` "only ever extends the sealed prefix as an episode continues" — times out at 5000ms, taking ~5.9–6.1s. Run in isolation it still takes 6127ms, so it's genuinely a slow test against a tight limit, not contention from the rest of the suite.

One inherent limitation worth flagging: a live model crew's request/response envelopes aren't representable in a `SavedGame` action log, so an arena run resumed from disk replays to the same tick with the deterministic crew rather than re-issuing the original model calls.
